subject: Being Heumann (Apple TV film)
query: is being heumann a true story
title: Is Being Heumann a true story? Yes, the 1977 disability rights sit-in
answer: Yes. "Being Heumann," streaming on Apple TV from Nov. 13, 2026, is based on the life of disability rights activist Judith "Judy" Heumann and her 2020 memoir of the same name. It centers on the real 1977 Section 504 sit-in, when disabled protesters occupied a federal building in San Francisco for nearly a month.
body:
The protest is real history. Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 barred discrimination against people with disabilities in any program that received federal money, but the government had not issued the rules needed to enforce it. On April 5, 1977, activists began sit-ins at federal offices around the country. The one in San Francisco's federal building was the only one that lasted: more than 100 people moved in, and a core group stayed for about four weeks (most accounts say 26 days). A delegation flew to Washington to press the case, and Health, Education and Welfare Secretary Joseph Califano signed the regulations on April 28, 1977. Heumann was one of the protest's leaders. Members of the Black Panther Party brought meals to the protesters, a detail the film also depicts.

Heumann, who had polio at 18 months old, was already known for suing New York City's school system in 1970 after it refused her a teaching license because she used a wheelchair. She later served as assistant secretary of education under President Bill Clinton and as a State Department adviser on disability rights under President Barack Obama. She died on March 4, 2023, at 75. Her memoir, "Being Heumann: An Unrepentant Memoir of a Disability Rights Activist," was written with Kristen Joiner.

The film is directed by Siân Heder, who won an Oscar for writing "CODA," and written by Heder and Rebekah Taussig. Ruth Madeley plays Heumann, and Mark Ruffalo plays Califano. Many other characters are based on real activists, including Kitty Cone (Madeline Delp), Ed Roberts (Michael Patrick Thornton) and Brad Lomax (Antwan Tolliver). Like most dramatizations, it compresses events: an A.V. Club review notes that the film's dramatic beats rewrite the long, slow occupation to suit the big screen. It runs 127 minutes and opened in select theaters on Nov. 6, 2026, before arriving on Apple TV.
in_the_news: "Being Heumann" begins streaming on Apple TV on Nov. 13, 2026, a week after a limited theatrical release.

faq.q: Is Being Heumann based on a book?
faq.a: Yes. It draws on Heumann's 2020 memoir, "Being Heumann: An Unrepentant Memoir of a Disability Rights Activist," co-written with Kristen Joiner.

faq.q: Who plays Judy Heumann in Being Heumann?
faq.a: British actor Ruth Madeley. Mark Ruffalo plays HEW Secretary Joseph Califano.

faq.q: Where can I watch Being Heumann?
faq.a: On Apple TV starting Nov. 13, 2026. It also played in select theaters from Nov. 6.

faq.q: How long did the 504 sit-in last?
